en: The Uṣṇīṣavijayā Dhāraṇī Sūtra, translated by the Śramaṇa Buddhāpāli of Kaśmīr by imperial decree:
Thus have I heard. At one time, the Bhagavat was staying at Śrāvastī, in the Jeta Grove.
At the Anāthapiṇḍada Garden,
together with a great assembly of one thousand two hundred and fifty bhikṣus,
and also with an assembly of twelve thousand great bodhisattvas.
At that time, in the assembly hall of the Sudharmā Hall in the Heaven of the Thirty-three,
there was a son of heaven named Sunetra,
who was wandering through the gardens and groves together with the great devas.
Furthermore, he was granted supreme nobility by Mahādeva;
surrounded before and behind by celestial maidens,
he joyfully engaged in play with various kinds of music.
They enjoyed themselves together, experiencing all manner of pleasures.
At that time, during the night, the Devaputra Susthita heard a voice say:
"The life of the Devaputra Susthita will come to an end in seven days."
After his life ended, he was reborn in Jambudvīpa;
there he underwent seven successive births as an animal,
and immediately thereafter experienced the sufferings of hell.
Having emerged from hell, he rarely attained a human body and was born into poverty and low status;
while still in the mother’s womb, he was born without both eyes.
At that time, the Devaputra Sunihita heard this voice.
He was immediately seized with great terror, the hair on his body standing on end; filled with sorrow and distress, he found no joy.
He hurried to the abode of Śakra, the Lord of Devas, wailing and weeping, overwhelmed by fear and at a loss for what to do.
Having prostrated to Śakra, the Honored One among Two-legged Beings, he addressed Śakra, saying: "Listen to what I have to say.
I am surrounded by various celestial maidens and enjoy all manner of pleasures."
He heard a voice say: "The Devaputra Susthitu’s life will come to an end in seven days.
After his death, he will be reborn in Jambudvīpa and undergo the body of an animal for seven successive lifetimes."
Having received these seven bodies, he immediately fell into the various hells.
Emerging from the hells, he rarely obtained a human body;
when born into a poor and lowly family, he was blind in both eyes.
"O Lord of Devas, how may I be delivered from this suffering?
When Śakra heard these words of the devaputra Susthita,
he was greatly astonished and immediately reflected within himself.
"What seven rebirths in the evil realms will this Devaputra Sunetra undergo?
At that time, Śakra remained in stillness for a moment, entered meditative concentration, and observed closely;
he then saw that Sunetra was destined to undergo seven rebirths in the evil realms.
That is to say, the bodies of pigs, dogs, jackals, monkeys, pythons, snakes, crows, vultures, and the like,
which consume various foul, evil, and impure things. At that time,
Śakra observed that the devaputra Susthita was destined to fall into the bodies of those who undergo seven cycles of rebirth within the evil realms.
My distress was extreme, and my heart was torn with pain.
Reflecting deeply, I found no way out; to whom could I turn for refuge?
There is only the Tathāgata, the Arhat, the Samyaksaṃbuddha.
May they be well-established so that they may be freed from this suffering.
At that time, during the first watch of the night on this very day,
Śakra took various flower garlands, unguents, and powdered incense.

Adorned with and holding exquisite celestial garments, he proceeded to the Jeta Grove and, having arrived at the place where the World-Honored One was, prostrated at the Buddha’s feet, circumambulated him seven times to the right,
and immediately made vast offerings before the Buddha.
Kneeling before the Buddha with palms joined, he addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One, how is it that the Devaputra Sunirmita shall undergo seven more rebirths in the evil realms of animals?
He related everything as previously described.
At that time, the Tathāgata emitted various kinds of light from the crown of his head,
which pervaded all worlds throughout the ten directions;
the light then returned and circled the Buddha three times.
It entered through the Buddha’s mouth.
The Buddha then smiled and addressed Śakra, saying:
"Devendra, there is a dhāraṇī called the 'Exalted and Victorious Uṣṇīṣa of the Tathāgata.'"
It can purify all evil realms;
it can thoroughly purify and eliminate all the suffering and affliction of birth and death;
and it can also thoroughly purify and eliminate the sufferings of the various hells, the realm of King Yama, and the animal kingdom.
Furthermore, it destroys all hells and can redirect one toward the auspicious paths.
O Lord of Devas, if there is anyone who hears this Uṣṇīṣavijayā Dhāraṇī but once with their ears, [it shall bring about such results].
All evil karma of the hells created in previous lives will be completely extinguished, and one shall obtain a pure body;
wherever one is born, one will remember and never forget.
From one buddha-field to another buddha-field,
from one celestial realm to another celestial realm,
they traveled throughout the Heaven of the Thirty-three.
In whatever place one is born, one shall remember and not forget it.
O Lord of Devas, if a person's life is about to end,
they should for a moment recollect this dhāraṇī.
Furthermore, one shall increase in longevity and attain purity of body, speech,
and mind; the body shall be free from pain and suffering,
and one shall find peace and security in every place according to one's merit and benefit.
Beheld by all Tathāgatas, constantly guarded by all celestial deities,
and revered by people, it causes malevolent obstacles to be extinguished.
All Bodhisattvas will with one mind protect and shelter him.
O Lord of Devas, if there is a person who can read and recite this dhāraṇī for even a moment,
all the sufferings of the hells, the animal realm, the realm of King Yama, and the hungry ghosts belonging to that person shall cease.
It destroys and annihilates them without leaving a trace,
including all Buddha-fields, the celestial palaces of the devas,
and all the gateways wherein bodhisattvas dwell.
Entering with ease and without obstruction according to his will,
Śakra then addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One, we pray only that the Tathāgata, for the sake of sentient beings..."
He spoke the method for increasing one's lifespan.
At that time, the World-Honored One, knowing the thoughts and intentions in the mind of Śakra,
understood his desire to hear the Buddha preach this dharani method.
Then he spoke the mantra, saying:
Namo bhagavate trailokyaprativiśiṣṭāya buddhāya bhagavate tadyathā...
Nye-ta oṃ viśodhaya samasama-samanta vāpasā spharaṇa gati-āgata svabhāva-viśuddhe abhiṣiñca tu māṃ. (10)

The Buddha addressed Śakra, saying:
This mantra is named the *Uṣṇīṣavijayā Dhāraṇī for Purifying All Evil Realms*.
It is capable of eliminating all obstacles such as sinful karma and the like,
and it is capable of shattering all the sufferings of the defiled evil realms.
"O Lord of Devas, this great dhāraṇī was proclaimed by eighty-eight hundred thousand koṭis of Ganges-sand Buddhas,
who together rejoiced in its acceptance and upholding."
The Tathāgata Mahāvairocana seals it with the Wisdom Seal (jñānamudrā).
This is for the purpose of destroying the suffering of the defiled evil realms of all sentient beings,
and for the sake of bringing liberation to all beings in the hells, the animal realm, and the world of King Yama.
It is for the sake of liberating those sentient beings who, facing urgent suffering and hardship, have fallen into the ocean of birth and death;
and for the sake of benefiting those sentient beings of short life and meager merit who lack protection, and those who delight in creating various defiled and evil karmas.
Furthermore, by the power of this dhāraṇī’s sustenance within Jambudvīpa,
it is able to cause sentient beings in the hells and evil realms—
who otherwise would transmigrate through various births and deaths— to [attain liberation].
It is for the sake of enabling those of little merit,
those sentient beings who do not believe in the retribution of good and evil karma, and those who have lost the right path,
to attain the meaning of liberation.
The Buddha told Śakra, Lord of Devas:
"I have spoken this dhāraṇī and entrust it to you.
You should transmit it to the Devaputra Susthita."
Furthermore, you should receive, uphold, read, recite, contemplate, cherish, remember,
and make offerings to it; and throughout Jambudvīpa,
you should extensively proclaim this dhāraṇī for the sake of all sentient beings.
I have also taught this dhāraṇī-seal for the sake of all the devaputras;
I entrust it to you, Śakra.
You should uphold and protect it well, ensuring that it is not forgotten or lost.
O Lord of Devas, if a person should hear this dhāraṇī for even a moment,
the heavy obstructions of evil karma accumulated over a thousand kalpas—
which would otherwise cause them to undergo various cycles of birth and death— shall be purified.
The realms of hell-beings, hungry ghosts, animals, and King Yama;
the bodies of asuras, yakṣas, rākṣasas, bhūtas, piśācas, pūtanas, kaṭapūtanas, and apasmārakas.
They shall no longer undergo rebirth in the bodies of mosquitoes, gadflies, turtles, dogs, pythons, snakes,
or any of the various birds; nor among the fierce beasts,
nor among any crawling or moving sentient beings, down to the level of an ant.
They will immediately attain rebirth in the assembly of the Buddhas, Tathāgatas, and Bodhisattvas who are in their final birth before Buddhahood;
or they will attain rebirth in a family of great Brahmins,
or in a family of the great Kṣatriya caste.
Or one may be born into a most excellent family of great nobility.
O Lord of Devas, that such persons are born in these aforementioned noble places is entirely due to having heard this dhāraṇī.
Wherever they are reborn, they shall all attain purity;
O Lord of Devas, up until their arrival at the most supreme site of the Bodhimanda,
it is entirely due to the merit of praising this dhāraṇī.
Thus, O Śakra, this dhāraṇī is named "Auspicious Purifier of All Evil Paths.
This is the Buddha-uṣṇīṣavijayā Dhāraṇī.
It is like the sun-treasury maṇi jewel:
pure and free from blemish, as pure as space,
its radiant flames shining through and pervading everywhere without exception.
If sentient beings uphold this dhāraṇī, it is likewise so;
they become as bright, pure, and supple as Jambūnada gold.
It causes people to behold it with joy and is not defiled by or attached to impurities.
O Lord of Devas, if there are sentient beings who uphold this dhāraṇī, they shall likewise be so.
By means of this wholesome purity, one shall attain rebirth in the good realms.
O Lord of Devas, wherever this dhāraṇī may be found, if one can transcribe it,
circulate it, receive and uphold it, recite and chant it, hear it, or make offerings to it—
One who is able to act in this way will find all evil realms completely purified,
and all the suffering and affliction of the hells will be utterly extinguished.
The Buddha told Śakra, Lord of Devas:
If a person can transcribe this dhāraṇī and place it atop a tall banner,
or upon a high mountain, or upon a multi-storied pavilion;
Even unto enshrining them within a stūpa,
O Lord of Devas, if there be bhikṣus, bhikṣuṇīs, upāsakas, upāsikās, or sons and daughters of noble family;
Either one sees [the dhāraṇī] upon banners and the like, or one is near it;
its shadow falls across the body,
or the dhāraṇī is blown by the wind.
When the dust atop the upper banners falls upon their bodies,
O Lord of Devas, all the karmic offenses of those sentient beings—

which would otherwise lead them to the suffering of the evil realms, such as the hells, the animal realm, the realm of King Yama, the realm of hungry ghosts, or the bodies of asuras— [shall be purified].
They do not receive anything at all, nor are they defiled by the stains of sin.
O Lord of Devas, such beings as these have been granted the prediction of enlightenment by all the Buddhas.
They all attain non-retrogression from *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*. O Great Emperor,
how much more so for those who further provide many kinds of offerings, such as flower garlands, unguents, powdered incense, banners, flags, canopies, robes, and necklaces.
Having created various adornments,
one should construct a stūpa at a crossroads and install the dhāraṇī therein.
With palms joined in reverence, they circumambulate, walk the path of practice, take refuge, and prostrate.
O Lord of Devas, those persons who can make such offerings are called Mahāsattvas.
Truly, you are a son of the Buddha and a pillar upholding the Dharma;
furthermore, this is a stūpa containing the entire bodily relics of the Tathāgata.
At that time, Yama, the King of Dharma—
Then, during the night, he came to where the Buddha was.
Having arrived, he adorned him with various celestial robes, exquisite flowers, and fragrant ointments;
having thus made offerings to the Buddha, he departed.
He circumambulated the Buddha seven times, prostrated at the Buddha’s feet, and spoke these words:
"I have heard that the Tathāgata has expounded and praised the Great Power Dhāraṇī; therefore, I have come here to practice and study it."
If there are those who receive, uphold, read, and recite this dhāraṇī,
I shall constantly follow and protect them,
ensuring that those who uphold it do not fall into hell.
Because they accord with the Tathāgata’s teaching, he protects and keeps them in mind.
At that time, the Four Great Kings, the World Protectors,
circumambulated the Buddha three times and addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One, I only pray that the Tathāgata will extensively explain for me the method for upholding this dhāraṇī.
At that time, the Buddha addressed the Four Heavenly Kings:
Listen attentively now;
I shall explain for you the method for receiving and upholding this dhāraṇī,
and I shall also explain it for the sake of all sentient beings with short lifespans.
One should first bathe and put on new, clean clothes; then,
on the fifteenth day of the waxing moon when the month is full,
one should observe the fast and recite this dhāraṇī.
Recite it one thousand times;
this will cause short-lived sentient beings to regain increased longevity,
forever leave behind the suffering of illness, and have all karmic obstructions completely extinguished.
All those in the various hells shall also attain liberation from their sufferings.
As for all classes of flying birds, animals, and sentient beings,
should this dhāraṇī but once pass through their ears, [they shall likewise be liberated].
Having exhausted this present body, one shall never again undergo rebirth.
The Buddha said: "If a person encounters a grave and malignant illness and hears this dhāraṇī..."
One will immediately attain permanent liberation from all diseases,
and one will also achieve the eradication and severance of those [karmic conditions] that would otherwise lead to rebirth in the evil realms.
One shall immediately attain rebirth in the world of tranquility.
From this body onward, one will never again receive a body born from a womb;
wherever one is born, one will be born by transformation within a lotus flower.
They remember all places of birth without forgetting and constantly know their past lives.
The Buddha said: "If a person has previously committed all manner of extremely grave evil karma..."
Thereupon, their lives will come to an end, and by virtue of these evil karmas, they shall fall into hell;
or they shall fall among the animals or into the realm of King Yama;
or they shall fall among the hungry ghosts, even falling into the Great Avīci Hell.
Whether they are born in the water or take on the bodies of various classes of birds and beasts,
one should take the bones from the deceased’s body and recite this dhāraṇī twenty-one times over a handful of earth.
Those whose bones have been scattered and lost shall immediately attain rebirth in heaven.
The Buddha said: "If a person can recite this dhāraṇī twenty-one times every day, they shall be worthy of receiving all the vast offerings of the world."
By relinquishing the body, one will be reborn in the Land of Ultimate Bliss.
If one constantly recites and contemplates [this], one will attain Great Nirvana;
furthermore, one's lifespan will be increased and one will experience supreme happiness.
Upon casting off this body, one will immediately attain rebirth in various subtle and wondrous Buddha-fields,
constantly meeting with all Buddhas in a single place,
where all Tathāgatas perpetually expound for them the subtle and profound meaning.
All the World-Honored Ones immediately conferred upon him this prediction.
The radiance of their bodies illuminated all buddha-fields.
The Buddha said: "If one recites this dharani according to the ritual method..."
First, take pure earth before that Buddha and construct an altar according to its required size,
making it square with four corners.
Scatter various kinds of grasses and flowers upon the altar,
burn many varieties of famous incense,
and kneel with the right knee touching the ground.
Constantly recollecting the Buddha in mind,
perform the Mūrdha-dhāraṇī mudrā by bending the index finger with the thumb.
Press the palms together against the heart.
Having recited this dhāraṇī one hundred and eight times, finish.
Within that maṇḍala, like a cloud-king raining down flowers,
one is able to universally make offerings to eighty-eight koṭis of Ganges-sand nayutas of hundreds of thousands of Buddhas.
Those Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, all praised him together, saying:
"Excellent! How rare! You are truly a son of the Buddha," and he immediately attained the samādhi of unobstructed wisdom.
One attains the Samādhi Adorned with the Great Bodhicitta.
The method for upholding this dhāraṇī should be as follows.
The Buddha told Śakra, Lord of Devas: "By means of this expedient, I [have taught it]."
It shall cause all sentient beings who are destined for the path of hell to attain liberation;
it shall also purify all evil realms.
Furthermore, it shall increase the lifespan of those who uphold it.
"Devānām-Indra, go and bestow this dhāraṇī of mine upon the prince Sudhana;
let it remain for seven full days."
"You and Sunetra have come together to see me.
At that time, Śakra, Lord of Devas, received this dharani method from the World-Honored One,
upheld it, and returned to his own celestial realm.
It was bestowed upon the Devaputra Susthita. At that time,
having received this dhāraṇī, the Devaputra Susthita...
For six days and six nights,
one should receive and maintain [the practice] according to the ritual; all vows will be fulfilled,
and one shall undergo all the sufferings of the evil realms and so forth.
He immediately attained liberation and dwelt upon the path to Bodhi.
His lifespan increased immeasurably, and with great joy, he cried out in a loud voice: "How rare is the Tathāgata!"
"How rare is this wondrous Dharma! How rare is its manifest efficacy!
It is most difficult to encounter, yet it has brought me liberation.
At that time, Śakra reached the seventh day.
Together with the divine son Sunirmita, he led a host of devas,
magnificently adorned with flower garlands, unguents, powdered incense, precious banners, streamers, parasols, celestial robes, and necklaces of exquisite beauty.
He went to where the Buddha was staying and prepared a great offering;
with exquisite celestial robes and various necklaces,
he made offerings to the World-Honored One and circumambulated him hundreds of thousands of times.
Standing before the Buddha, they leaped for joy and sat down to listen to the Dharma.
At that time, the World-Honored One extended his golden arm and stroked the crown of the head of the Devaputra Susthitamati.
He then preached the Dharma to them and bestowed upon them the prediction of enlightenment.
The Buddha said, "This sutra is named the *Uṣṇīṣavijayā Dhāraṇī for Purifying All Evil Realms*.
You should receive and uphold it."
At that time, the great assembly, having heard the Dharma, rejoiced, believed, accepted, and practiced it.
